page: OVHcloud c3-32 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor running on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 25%, raw memory bandwidth read and write tests for large uncached blocks remain in the average tier. Text processing and bzip3 decompression tasks demonstrate strong execution speeds, whereas database operations and static web serving throughput align with average performance tiers.

The server offers a high physical core density with dedicated CPU allocation, which avoids resource contention. However, the 2.0 GB of memory per core represents a lower RAM-to-CPU ratio, making it less suitable for memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of local NVMe storage and dedicated AMD EPYC cores provides a balanced resource profile for compute-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. This instance is suited for multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, text processing, and moderate-scale web serving or database operations.
